label: Majhi Punjabi
region: Majha — Amritsar / Tarn Taran belt, Punjab
uncertainty: Exact neighbourhood slang varies between Amritsar city and village Majha; rural register is used unless the user selects urban.
Kinship tone after conflict is contested in some families; Bebe remains the default maternal address.

ADAM.work: college student expected to inherit the family kiryana shop

MOTHER.work: runs the household and keeps the shop accounts in a register

SISTER.work: helps Bebe; applying for a teaching post in the nearby school

FRIEND.work: drives a small tempo; Adam's childhood yaar from the same pind

UNCLE.work: owns the village kiryana shop on the main chowk

HOUSE FRONT YARD.architecture: Brick kothi with a small aangan, iron gate that never latches, peepal shade at the wall, charpai against the verandah
HOUSE FRONT YARD.urban_variant: Narrow front courtyard of a lane house near Hall Bazaar, Amritsar

KITCHEN.architecture: Smoke-darkened rasoi with a gas stove, steel glasses, aluminium kettle, and a wooden almirah of masala tins
KITCHEN.urban_variant: Compact tiled kitchen in a two-room city house

MARKET STREET.architecture: Open mandi road with kiryana, cycle-repair, and a reri of kulche-chole; buses throw dust
MARKET STREET.urban_variant: Katra street near Hall Bazaar with denser shopfronts

LIVING ROOM.architecture: Baithak with one sofa, floor dari, framed family photograph, and a low table for the letter
LIVING ROOM.urban_variant: Front room with a TV cabinet and the same low table

props.letter: unopened envelope from Mama Jagtar, written in blue ballpoint
props.lamp: single tube light plus a table lamp in the baithak

ADAM.garments: White khaddar kurta, navy pajama, faded cotton jacket, leather juttis
ADAM.grooming: Unshorn hair tied under a navy parna, light stubble

MOTHER.garments: Cotton salwar kameez in maroon, contrasting phulkari-border dupatta covering the head indoors and out
MOTHER.jewellery: Gold hoops, thin gold chain, white chooda-style bangles kept simple
MOTHER.grooming: Grey-streaked hair in a bun, sindoor not emphasised

SISTER.garments: Mint kameez, white salwar, lightweight printed dupatta, no heavy makeup
SISTER.jewellery: Small studs and a thin black thread bracelet

FRIEND.garments: Checked shirt over a vest, cargo-style pajama, cloth cap rather than a full turban

food: paratha and achar in the rasoi
sound: distant Gurbani from a nearby gurdwara at morning

gestures.greeting: Palms together or a light sat sri akaal; younger people lower their eyes first with Bebe
gestures.respect: Do not sit in Bebe's chair until she nods; cover the head in the baithak when the matter is serious
gestures.conflict: Voices rise, then drop; public refusal is avoided; truth is expected inside the rasoi and baithak
gestures.touch: Sister may catch a sleeve; Friend does not touch Bebe; Mother may hold the letter rather than the son

humour: Dry teasing (yaar, lost a bet) rather than slapstick; never use dialect as the joke
kinship_rules: Children address mother as Bebe, not Mum or Mummy, unless urban code-switch is approved.
Mother's brother is Mama, never Uncle in adapted dialogue.
Friend is yaar, not a kinship term.

story_world.stakes: Leaving college for the kiryana shop is not only a job choice; it is izzat in the pind and the mother's brother's trust.
story_world.community: Neighbours already speak as if Jaswant will take the shop. Public refusal would travel faster than the letter.
story_world.resolution: Reading the letter together restores the household as the place where decisions are made, without forcing him to accept the shop.
